Subject: Recap: procurement & billing next steps (PO vs marketplace, e-invoice)

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you into a quick pilot without surprises on the billing side: 

1) Commercial path options we discussed
   - Direct PO to Redwood Inference (preferred by your procurement).
   - Marketplace purchase (AWS/Azure) — fine if you later decide to move; affects invoicing flow.

2) Billing & invoice preferences we need to confirm from your side
   - Billing entity and exact remit-to address (for PO and invoice header).
   - Tax ID / EIN (for our accounts payable).
   - Desired payment terms (net-30/45/60) and whether a credit application is required.
   - Whether Oakridge requires an e-invoice (XML) template — if yes, we can provide a sample mapping.

3) Attachments I'm including for reference (attached to this thread): Redwood sales deck (overview), and a W-9 for your vendor records.

Next steps I propose:
 - If you will go direct PO, please send the PO to billing@redwood.ai and cc me; our billing ops will validate the PO fields.
 - If you need an e-invoice sample (xml), reply and I will loop in Kimberly from Billing Ops who will share the file and the field mapping.
 - If you want net terms, we can start a short credit-app — I can share the link now.

If helpful I can also produce a one-page commercial order form for DocuSign to accelerate procurement.

Thanks again — I’ll wait for confirmation on the billing entity and whether AP prefers PO vs marketplace so Kimberly can prep the e-invoice sample.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0173

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from procurement/AP here: 

- Oakridge will most likely proceed with a direct PO for the pilot. AP needs the vendor payee name and remit address exactly as it should appear on invoices.
- We operate on net-30 by default for pilots; would Redwood accept net-30? We can complete a credit app if required.
- For tax purposes: Oakridge is US-based (no VAT). We will need Redwood’s EIN and a W-9 on file.
- AP prefers electronic invoices where possible — can you share a sample e-invoice XML (we have an automated parser). If you have a mapping doc that lists which XML fields map to our PO/invoice fields, that would be ideal.

AP contact (cc'd): ap@oakridge.com — please loop them in on next steps so they can expect the PO and any required documentation.

Thanks,
Susan Evans
Senior Procurement Manager
Oakridge Analytics

Hi Susan —

Kimberly from Billing Ops here; thanks for the quick reply. I attached a short sample XML e-invoice and a vendor W-9 for Oakridge to keep on file. Notes below to make the PO/invoice handoff smooth: 

- Vendor information (please use exactly):
  Redwood Inference, Inc.
  EIN: 12-3456789
  Remit-to: 120 Market St, Suite 300, San Francisco, CA 94105
  billing@redwood.ai

- Net terms: we can support net-30 for this pilot provided we have a signed PO and a completed credit-app (link below). If Oakridge prefers to proceed first and then supply a PO, we can accept an initial pro-forma invoice and then exchange a PO within 7 days.

- E-invoice: attached is oakridge_einvoice_sample.xml — the mapping in the XML uses standard fields: InvoiceNumber, InvoiceDate, BuyerPO, LineItem[Sku/Description/Qty/UnitPrice], TaxAmount, InvoiceTotal. If your parser expects different element names let us know and we can adapt.

- Marketplace note: if later moved to AWS Marketplace, invoices will come from the marketplace provider and payments route may change; that does not change usage reports but will alter the remit-to.

Attachments: redwood_W9.pdf (W-9 stub), oakridge_einvoice_sample.xml (e-invoice sample stub).

Links: Credit app: https://redwood.ai/credit-app/DEAL-8932

Happy to hop on a 15-min call with AP if that helps to validate the XML fields.

Best,
